title: Find two-term representations by quotient dictionaries
summary: Replaces an all-pairs loop with one pass of exact dictionary insertions, plus vector normalization/key costs. Applies directly to finite-field coding searches, sparse decompositions, and any explicit dictionary over a field.
content: Given nonzero target T, choose a linear functional c with c(T)=1 and set q(v)=v-c(v)T. Normalize each nonzero q(v) to a canonical projective key, scaling c(v) by the same factor. Two proper vectors span T exactly when their quotient keys match and their scaled anchor values differ. If the normalizers are lambda_v, lambda_w and the anchor difference is D, the witness is T=(lambda_v/D)v-(lambda_w/D)w. Handle q=0 separately: a nonzero anchor is a one-term hit; zero anchor is the zero vector.
whenToUse: Replaces an all-pairs loop with one pass of exact dictionary insertions, plus vector normalization/key costs. Applies directly to finite-field coding searches, sparse decompositions, and any explicit dictionary over a field.
limitations: Matching quotient keys alone is insufficient. Preserve target-coordinate deviations even when off-target coordinates vanish. Hash collisions must be resolved by exact quotient-key comparison or reconstruction, retaining unequal keys separately; replay recovered witnesses on original coordinates. Expected linear dictionary operations do not remove candidate-generation, vector-size, or memory costs. The general-target statement is the same elementary argument; production code specializes field and target encodings.
